title: Whole Milk 1 gal

drivers.name: Price increase (5.1%)
drivers.evidence: Two recent weeks at $4.56 saw sales 10% and 42% below baseline; 30% off in Halloween week showed no lift, indicating high price sensitivity.

drivers.name: TikTok trend
drivers.evidence: No past event matches this driver; noise-adjusted estimate for untested viral trends is x1.10, but evidence is weak (one past occurrence, no sales data).

adjustment.analysis: The baseline median is 207.6. A price increase to $4.56 (+5.1%) is present, but recent weeks at this price (2026-09-28, 2026-10-05) saw sales of 195 and 119—well below baseline. The 10% off promotion in Jan 2026 lifted sales to x1.56, but the 30% off Halloween week saw no lift (x0.95), suggesting price sensitivity. The TikTok trend is unproven; no past event matches this driver. No events or promotions are scheduled. The classical model's x1.0 is a starting point. Given strong price sensitivity and no uplift evidence at this price, a small downside is justified. The TikTok trend is uncertain and unvalidated.

  events: none
  shelf price: 4.56 (+5.1% vs regular price 4.34)
  planner notes: Product is trending on TikTok

STATISTICAL BASELINE (exponential smoothing of recent sales; it ignores events, promotions and prices):
  median 207.6 | 5%-95%: 133.5 - 290.3 | 10%-90%: 156.3 - 281.1

In the evidence below, 'vs baseline' = actual units / what this same baseline predicted for that week.
It is the multiplier that would have been right, so it maps directly onto median_multiplier.
This product's ordinary weeks already swing about +/-22% around the baseline, so a past effect smaller than that, seen only a few times, is mostly noise. The
'noise-adjusted estimate' is the effect shrunk toward x1.0 for that noise and the number of sightings.
